newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Thai prime minister arrives for Indonesia visit.
newsitem.headline: Thai prime minister arrives for Indonesia visit.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh arrived in Indonesia on Thursday for a two-day visit and talks with the region's elder statesman, President Suharto.
Chavalit was greeted at Jakarta's Halim Perdanakusuma airbase by Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas. They drove to the presidential palace for a formal welcome.

Diplomatic sources said the visit was primarily a courtesy call, following a custom of new leaders of members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) first calling on fellow ASEAN states.
Suharto, Indonesia's leader since the mid-1960s, is a co-founder of ASEAN and one of the world's longest-serving heads of state.
ASEAN comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.
Chavalit, who took office in November after general elections in Thailand, has personal ties to Indonesia. His wife Phanklua was born there and later emigrated to Thailand.
Thai diplomatic sources said there were no outstanding issues between Bangkok and Jakarta.
"They will have open-ended discussions, but there are no particular issues," one source said. The talks would cover bilateral relations and cooperation in various areas.
Chavalit will attend with a state banquet hosted by Suharto in the evening.
The two sides will hold bilateral talks on Friday morning before the Thai party leaves.
